response:
Final-round diagnosis. The archive has settled a sequence of sharp questions. (i) The mechanism is *unforced cheapness*: an unencumbered-claim valuation leg gated on the cash stock relative to the demands on cash. (ii) The cash stock is essential and not interchangeable with profitability — swapping the cash numerator for a cash-earnings flow at identical denominator and units collapsed alpha from +6.3% to +1.8% (t 1.71). (iii) Rank transformation is essential — the same economics as a raw monotone ratio produced −2.2%. (iv) Broadening the cheapness side raises the cross-sectional slope (consensus leg: fmb 5.01, Sharpe 0.477) while the additive combination raises reliability (t 5.11 at +6.0%). (v) The liability-timing gate has the highest slope of all (fmb 5.19) but a smaller alpha (+3.1%), suggesting asset-side and liability-side freedom are complementary. (vi) The one unresolved defect is the short side: correct, large, reliable alphas (−5.4%, t −5.09) with a flat Fama-MacBeth slope, because a non-negative rank product leaves cheap firms pooled at zero. This batch finalises the long side on the two best structural forms (S1, S2, S6), tests the two remaining substantive questions — coverage cost of multi-year averaging (S3) and whether the gate is burn horizon or plain cash intensity (S5) — and repairs the short-side slope defect (S4).

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Four-Channel Unforced Cheapness Score
EXPRESSION: IND_RANK(SUMRANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), SUMRANK(RATIO(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(che, cogs))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheapness evidenced by three independent accounting bases and freedom from forced transaction are partial substitutes: a deeper discount can offset a shorter runway and a longer runway can justify a smaller discount, so an evenly weighted score across the unencumbered claim, gross profit, cash earnings and the survival horizon should identify mispricing more reliably than any conjunctive gate.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The additive form of three channels produced the archive's most reliable result (+6.0%, t 5.11) and the consensus multiplicative form produced its best Sharpe (0.477) and slope (5.01); this pairs the better operator with the better channel set, and the balanced nesting gives each pair equal weight rather than the lopsided weights the critic identified in the earlier nesting. Because no channel can zero out the score, portfolio composition stays broad and stable, which is what generated the high t-statistic in the additive design.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Consensus Cheapness With Dual Cash Gate
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), MUL(prcc_f, csho))))), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(che, cogs), RATIO(che, ADD(dltt, dlc)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Operations and creditors are separate claimants on the same cash, and a firm is unforced when its cash is ample against both; combining the two demands as ranked channels — rather than summing them in one denominator where operating costs swamp debt, or taking their minimum — measures overall freedom without discarding either constraint.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Both gates independently deliver alphas above 4.9% with t-statistics above 4.2 on this valuation leg, and the earlier attempts to unite them failed for construction reasons the archive has now diagnosed: the summed denominator was dominated by cost of goods sold, while the minimum operator cut coverage to 0.104. Ranking each demand separately before combining keeps both economically live and preserves coverage at the 0.118 level of the leading signals.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: High-Coverage Consensus With Survival Horizon
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, cogs)))
HYPOTHESIS: The unencumbered claim and the gross-profit stream together describe cheapness well enough that the multi-year averaged cash-earnings channel is redundant; dropping it should preserve the mispricing signal while restoring the fifth of the sample that the three-year averaging requirement removes.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every leading signal in the archive sits at coverage 0.118 purely because of the MA(ib+dp,3) term, while the gross-profit-yield version of the same gate reaches 0.140 with the archive's highest slope (fmb 7.71), so this tests whether statistical power can be bought back without sacrificing the claim-based alpha. It is the single most consequential remaining specification question, since a comparable alpha at 0.14 coverage would strictly dominate the current champion.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Signed Cheapness With A Funding Gap
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(dlc, che), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: A cash shortfall against maturing debt destroys shareholder value in richly priced firms but is partly already discounted in cheap ones, so the funding gap should be scored against a signed measure of expensiveness: expensive firms with a gap are the strongest shorts while cheap firms with a gap are merely fairly priced, not neutral.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The archived funding-gap signal delivered −5.4% at t −5.09 but a flat cross-sectional slope of −0.38, because its non-negative rank product pools all cheap firms near zero and gives the Fama-MacBeth regression no variation to exploit on that side. Replacing the expensiveness rank with an industry z-score makes the score signed and monotone across the whole cross-section, which should align the slope evidence with the portfolio evidence without altering the economics.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Consensus Cheapness With Cash Intensity
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), MUL(prcc_f, csho))))), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, at)))
HYPOTHESIS: If what the market underprices is simply the presence of a large cash balance rather than the number of months of operations it funds, then scaling cash by total assets should gate the discount as effectively as scaling it by the operating cost base.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every successful gate in the archive scales cash by a measure of demands — operating costs, total debt, current liabilities — so the survival-horizon interpretation has never been tested against the simplest alternative, cash intensity, which contains no demand term at all. A comparable alpha would mean the mechanism is a cash-holdings valuation effect, while a materially weaker one would confirm that the horizon, not the hoard, is what separates quality value from traps.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Consensus Cheapness Free On Both Sides
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), MUL(prcc_f, csho))))), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(che, cogs), NEG(RATIO(dlc, at)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Freedom from forced transaction has an asset side and a liability side — cash sufficient to fund operations, and no debt falling due that a lender can call — and a cheap firm secure on both counts is the purest form of quality value.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: These two gates are the archive's complementary extremes on the same valuation leg: the runway delivers the largest alpha (+6.3%, t 4.94) while the absence of near-term maturities delivers the largest cross-sectional slope (fmb 5.19) with a smaller alpha, so combining them targets the metric each one lacks. Current debt scaled by assets is defined and equal to zero for debt-free firms, so the combined gate adds no coverage cost and no explosive ratio, unlike the earlier cash-denominated maturity measures.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---CRITIQUE Four-Channel Unforced Cheapness Score---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: This is the literal union of two archived signals — "Additive Unforced Cheapness Score" (claim + cash earnings + runway) and the gross-profit channel from "Consensus Cheapness With Survival Horizon" — so it is an incremental re-nesting rather than a new mechanism, and with four highly correlated price-scaled channels the marginal information from the added leg is likely near zero.

---CRITIQUE Consensus Cheapness With Dual Cash Gate---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The two "demands" being combined share the same numerator (che) and are therefore strongly correlated, so the additive gate is close to a monotone transform of the archived runway gate; additionally the claim that coverage is preserved at 0.118 is doubtful since the che/(dltt+dlc) component already cost the archived creditor-proof variant coverage (0.106) through zero/missing-debt denominators.

---CRITIQUE High-Coverage Consensus With Survival Horizon---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The motivating premise is factually wrong — the binding coverage constraint is the (act − lt) claim term, which caps archived act−lt signals at ~0.121, not the MA(ib+dp,3) term, so dropping cash earnings buys at best 0.003 of coverage while discarding a channel that the archive shows carries alpha.

---CRITIQUE Signed Cheapness With A Funding Gap---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: This is a defensible construction fix for a genuinely diagnosed slope/alpha divergence (non-negative rank products give the FMB regression no signed variation), and the expected negative sign matches the expression's direction, though the un-winsorized IND_ZSCORE of a market-cap-scaled claim yield is severely fat-tailed and will let a handful of micro-cap outliers dominate the cross-sectional slope.

---CRITIQUE Consensus Cheapness With Cash Intensity---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A clean, honestly framed ablation that discriminates "survival horizon" from a plain cash-holdings effect (itself a known published anomaly, Palazzo 2012), which limits novelty but makes the test genuinely informative about which mechanism drives the archive's champions.

---CRITIQUE Consensus Cheapness Free On Both Sides---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: The two gate components are economically and statistically complementary (asset-side runway with the largest alpha, liability-side maturity absence with the largest slope) rather than redundant like the dual-cash version, the coverage argument is correct since dlc/at is defined for debt-free firms, and the expression matches the stated hypothesis and sign.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Additive Score With Liability-Side Freedom
EXPRESSION: IND_RANK(SUMRANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), NEG(RATIO(dlc, at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheapness and freedom from creditor-imposed deadlines are substitutes rather than complements: a firm with no debt falling due needs less of a discount to be attractive, and a deeply discounted claim can tolerate some maturity pressure, so the two should be scored additively rather than through a conjunctive gate.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: The additive operator produced the archive's most reliable alpha (+6.0%, t 5.11) using cash-based liquidity as its third channel, while the liability-timing channel has only ever been used multiplicatively, where it delivered the archive's highest cross-sectional slope (fmb 5.19) but a smaller alpha (+3.1%) — so substituting it into the validated additive structure tests whether that slope strength survives when the channel can no longer be zeroed out. Unlike a fourth price-scaled cheapness channel, current debt over assets is not collinear with the other two legs and is defined at zero for debt-free firms, so it adds genuinely independent variation without any coverage cost.
REASONING_END

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Consensus Cheapness With Held And Convertible Resources
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), MUL(prcc_f, csho))))), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(che, cogs), RATIO(act, at))))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm avoids forced transaction either because it already holds the cash or because a large share of its assets can be converted into cash quickly; these are distinct resources — one immediate, one realisable — and a cheap firm possessing both is the least likely to be a trap.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This replaces the two same-numerator cash demands, which were close to a monotone transform of each other, with two liquidity channels built from different balance-sheet quantities: cash against the annual burn, and the current-asset share of the asset base, which independently delivered +1.9% alpha against a plain book-to-market leg. Neither channel involves a debt denominator, so the coverage erosion that afflicted the creditor-proof variant at 0.106 cannot occur and the signal should hold the 0.118 coverage of the leading constructs.
REASONING_END

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Earnings-Based Cheapness With Survival Horizon
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, cogs)))
HYPOTHESIS: If the survival horizon is the true source of abnormal return, it should convert ordinary earnings-based cheapness — cash earnings and gross profit relative to price — into alpha without any balance-sheet claim term, since what matters is that the firm cannot be forced to transact rather than what its liquidation value happens to be.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The coverage ceiling in this archive comes from the net-current-asset claim term, which caps every claim-based signal near 0.121 while runway-gated earnings yields reach 0.140, so removing the claim leg rather than the averaged earnings leg is the correct way to test the coverage-versus-content trade-off. It is also the decisive attribution test for the whole research line: gross-profit yield alone under this gate gave +2.9% at t 2.94, so a materially larger alpha here would show the cash-earnings channel matters independently, while a similar one would confirm the unencumbered claim is doing the economic work.
REASONING_END
